# Incremental Effects of Narrative Identity and Traits on Mental Health: A Nine-Year Longitudinal Study

## Data analysis and results

This markdown file reproduces the analyses reported in "Incremental
Effects of Narrative Identity and Traits on Mental Health: A Nine-Year
Longitudinal Study" by Majse Lind, Sebnem Ture, Dan P. McAdams, and
Henry R. Cowan.

Note that this set of analyses is on preprocessed data. Unprocessed data
and a preprocessing script are also available on the project OSF site,
along with README documentation: <https://osf.io/27qc9/>

Inquiries regarding this project can be directed to Majse Lind at
[mlind\@ikp.aau.dk](mailto:mlind@ikp.aau.dk){.email}

# Descriptive stats

## Demographics

See manuscript **"Participants and procedures"** section.

```{r demographics setup}
# Confirm that all pts have at least 2 coded narrative data points
IDs <- ylc %>% 
  drop_na(ac_val) %>% 
  select(ID) %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  filter(n() > 1) %>% #Drop pts with 0 or 1 coded narratives
  distinct(ID) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() 

# Filter pts with narrative data and select baseline data
bl_data <- ylc %>% 
  filter(ID %in% IDs$ID) %>% 
  select(ID, year, "t1: date of birth (dd-mmm-year)", "date completed interview (dd-mmm-year)",
         "t1: sex of respondent", "highest level of education completed", "race/ethnicity") %>%
  filter(year==1) 
```

### Age at baseline

```{r age}
lubridate::time_length(difftime(bl_data$`date completed interview (dd-mmm-year)`, bl_data$`t1: date of birth (dd-mmm-year)`), unit = "years") %>%
  round(1) %>%
  describe()
```

### Self-reported sex at baseline (count and %)

0 = Male 1 = Female

```{r sex}
rbind(table(bl_data$`t1: sex of respondent`), round(table(bl_data$`t1: sex of respondent`)/nrow(bl_data)*100, 1)) #Table with count and %
```

### Education at baseline (count and %)

1 = High School 2 = Some college 3 = College (B.A. or B.S.) 4 = Graduate
work (post-college) 5 = Other

```{r edu}
rbind(table(bl_data$`highest level of education completed`), round(table(bl_data$`highest level of education completed`)/nrow(bl_data)*100, 1)) #Table with count and %
```

### Race/ethnicity (count and %)

1 = White/Caucasian 2 = African-American 5 = Interracial 6 = Other

```{r race}
rbind(table(bl_data$`race/ethnicity`), round(table(bl_data$`race/ethnicity`)/nrow(bl_data)*100, 1)) #Table with count and %
```

# Growth curve models (multilevel models in {lme4})

First, we define a function to run a sequence of growth curve models for each predictor and outcome.

```{r mlm function}
ylc_models <- function(outcome, predictor, data){
  # Confirm that only pts with narrative data are included
  data <- data  %>% 
    select(ID, year_cent5, extra_z, neur_z, open_z, consc_z, agree_z, outcome, 
           paste0(predictor, "_pmean"), paste0(predictor, "_pmc"),
           end_val_pmean, end_val_pmc) %>%
    drop_na() %>% 
    group_by(ID) %>%
    filter(n() > 1) %>%
    ungroup()
    
  # Build list of models
  output <- list()
  
  # Simple growth curve model
  output$gc <- lmer(as.formula(paste0(outcome, "~ year_cent5 + (1 + year_cent5 | ID)")), data, 
                    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 99999)))
  
  # Narrative identity model with interactions with time
  output$ni_int <- lmer(as.formula(paste0(outcome, "~ year_cent5 * ", paste0(predictor, "_pmean"), " + ", paste0(predictor, "_pmc"),  "+ end_val_pmean * year_cent5 + end_val_pmc + (1 + year_cent5 | ID)")), data, 
                        control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 99999)))
  
  # Traits model with interactions with time
  output$tr_int <- lmer(as.formula(paste0(outcome, "~ year_cent5 * extra_z + year_cent5 * neur_z + year_cent5 * open_z + year_cent5 * consc_z + year_cent5 * agree_z + (1 + year_cent5 | ID)")), data, 
                        control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 99999)))
  
  # Full model with narrative identity and traits, with interactions with time
  output$all_int <- lmer(as.formula(paste0(outcome, "~ year_cent5 + end_val_pmc + ", paste0(predictor, "_pmc")," + extra_z + neur_z + open_z + consc_z + agree_z + end_val_pmean + ", paste0(predictor, "_pmean")," + year_cent5 * extra_z + year_cent5 * neur_z + year_cent5 * open_z + year_cent5 * consc_z + year_cent5 * agree_z + year_cent5 * end_val_pmean + year_cent5 * ", paste0(predictor, "_pmean"), " + (1 + year_cent5 | ID)")), data, 
                         control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 99999)))
  # Return list of models
  return(output)
}
```

## Combined agency/communion models

These are the main models reported in **Tables 3 and 4**.

First we create all models using the function we defined above.

```{r ac models}
bdi_ac_mods <- ylc_models("bdi_sz", "ac_val", ylc)
wb_ac_mods <- ylc_models("wb_comp", "ac_val", ylc)
```

Then we compare model fit. The models are nested: models 2 and 3 are
nested within model 4; and model 1 is nested within models 2 and 3. To
test differences in fit for nested models, this gives us two model
sequences: 
- Model 1 \> Model 2 \> Model 4 
- Model 1 \> Model 3 \> Model 4

We will test each of these model sequences for depression first. These
models are reported in **Table 3**, with tests of improvements in model fit
shown in the χ2 comparisons column.

```{r ac dep model comps}
bdi_ac_mods[setdiff(names(bdi_ac_mods), "ni_int")] %>% #Drop model "ni_int" from model sequence
  with(do.call(anova, lapply(names(.), as.name))) #Compare models 

bdi_ac_mods[setdiff(names(bdi_ac_mods), "tr_int")] %>% #Drop model "tr_int" from model sequence
  with(do.call(anova, lapply(names(.), as.name))) #Compare models
```

Now we will test each of these model sequences for well-being. These
models are reported in **Table 3**, with tests of improvements in model fit shown in the χ2 comparisons column.

```{r ac wb model comps}
wb_ac_mods[setdiff(names(wb_ac_mods), "ni_int")] %>%
  with(do.call(anova, lapply(names(.), as.name)))
wb_ac_mods[setdiff(names(wb_ac_mods), "tr_int")] %>%
  with(do.call(anova, lapply(names(.), as.name)))
```

Next, we will examine Model 4, the full NI + traits model. This output
appears in **Table 4**. Note: cent5 = "centered on Year 5"; "pmean" =
person-mean, aka. between-person; "pmc" = person-mean-centered, aka.
within-person

First we will examine the depression model.

```{r ac dep model}
tab_model(bdi_ac_mods$all_int, show.intercept = F, collapse.ci = F)
```

Next we will examine the well-being model.

```{r ac wb model}
tab_model(wb_ac_mods$all_int, show.intercept = F, collapse.ci = F)
```

## Models with agency only

Because agency and communion are often examined separately in the
narrative identity literature, we also provide models with effects for
agency and communion tested independently. First, the following models
present the same output as above, for agency only.

First we run all the models:

```{r agn models}
bdi_agn_mods <- ylc_models("bdi_sz", "agn_val0", ylc)
wb_agn_mods <- ylc_models("wb_comp", "agn_val0", ylc)
```

Then we compare model fit. These comparisons parallel the comparisons
for agency/communion above, and are reported in Supplement **Table S1.1**.

Model fit comparisons for depression:

```{r agn dep model comps}
bdi_agn_mods[setdiff(names(bdi_agn_mods), "ni_int")] %>% #Drop model "ni_int" from comparison
  with(do.call(anova, lapply(names(.), as.name))) #Compare models using anova() function
bdi_agn_mods[setdiff(names(bdi_agn_mods), "tr_int")] %>%
  with(do.call(anova, lapply(names(.), as.name)))
```

Model fit comparisons for well-being:

```{r agn wb model comps}
wb_agn_mods[setdiff(names(wb_agn_mods), "ni_int")] %>%
  with(do.call(anova, lapply(names(.), as.name)))
wb_agn_mods[setdiff(names(wb_agn_mods), "tr_int")] %>%
  with(do.call(anova, lapply(names(.), as.name)))
```

Next, we examine Model 4 for agency. These results are presented in
Supplement **Table S1.2**.

Depression model:

```{r agn dep model}
tab_model(bdi_agn_mods$all_int, show.intercept = F, collapse.ci = F)
```

Well-being model:

```{r agn wb model}
tab_model(wb_agn_mods$all_int, show.intercept = F, collapse.ci = F)
```

## Models excluding ending valence

Finally, models were also calculated without ending valence. First, the model function was modified to drop ending valence from all models.

```{r mlm function no ev}
ylc_models_no_ev <- function(outcome, predictor, data){
  # Confirm that only pts with narrative data are included
  data <- data  %>% 
    select(ID, year_cent5, extra_z, neur_z, open_z, consc_z, agree_z, outcome, 
           paste0(predictor, "_pmean"), paste0(predictor, "_pmc")) %>%
    drop_na() %>% 
    group_by(ID) %>%
    filter(n() > 1) %>%
    ungroup()
    
  # Build list of models
  output <- list()
  
  # Simple growth curve model
  output$gc <- lmer(as.formula(paste0(outcome, "~ year_cent5 + (1 + year_cent5 | ID)")), data, 
                    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 99999)))
  
  # Narrative identity model with interactions with time
  output$ni_int <- lmer(as.formula(paste0(outcome, "~ year_cent5 * ", paste0(predictor, "_pmean"), " + ", paste0(predictor, "_pmc"),  "+ (1 + year_cent5 | ID)")), data, 
                        control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 99999)))
  
  # Traits model with interactions with time
  output$tr_int <- lmer(as.formula(paste0(outcome, "~ year_cent5 * extra_z + year_cent5 * neur_z + year_cent5 * open_z + year_cent5 * consc_z + year_cent5 * agree_z + (1 + year_cent5 | ID)")), data, 
                        control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 99999)))
  
  # Full model with narrative identity and traits, with interactions with time
  output$all_int <- lmer(as.formula(paste0(outcome, "~ year_cent5 + ", paste0(predictor, "_pmc")," + extra_z + neur_z + open_z + consc_z + agree_z + ", paste0(predictor, "_pmean")," + year_cent5 * extra_z + year_cent5 * neur_z + year_cent5 * open_z + year_cent5 * consc_z + year_cent5 * agree_z + year_cent5 * ", paste0(predictor, "_pmean"), " + (1 + year_cent5 | ID)")), data, 
                         control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 99999)))
  # Return list of models
  return(output)
}
```

Then we create all models using this modified function.

```{r ac models no ev}
bdi_ac_mods_no_ev <- ylc_models_no_ev("bdi_sz", "ac_val", ylc)
wb_ac_mods_no_ev <- ylc_models_no_ev("wb_comp", "ac_val", ylc)
```

Then we compare model fit. Model fit is shown in Supplement **Table S3.1**. First we compare depression models:

```{r ac dep model comps no ev}
bdi_ac_mods_no_ev[setdiff(names(bdi_ac_mods_no_ev), "ni_int")] %>% #Drop model "ni_int" from model sequence
  with(do.call(anova, lapply(names(.), as.name))) #Compare models 

bdi_ac_mods_no_ev[setdiff(names(bdi_ac_mods_no_ev), "tr_int")] %>% #Drop model "tr_int" from model sequence
  with(do.call(anova, lapply(names(.), as.name))) #Compare models
```

Then we test each of the well-being models. Supplement **Table S3.1** reports these results.

```{r ac wb model comps no ev}
wb_ac_mods_no_ev[setdiff(names(wb_ac_mods_no_ev), "ni_int")] %>%
  with(do.call(anova, lapply(names(.), as.name)))
wb_ac_mods_no_ev[setdiff(names(wb_ac_mods_no_ev), "tr_int")] %>%
  with(do.call(anova, lapply(names(.), as.name)))
```

Finally, we examine Model 4, the full NI + traits model. This output
appears in Supplement **Table S3.2**. Note: cent5 = "centered on Year 5"; "pmean" =
person-mean, aka. between-person; "pmc" = person-mean-centered, aka.
within-person

First we will examine the depression model.

```{r ac dep model no ev}
tab_model(bdi_ac_mods_no_ev$all_int, show.intercept = F, collapse.ci = F)
```

Next we will examine the well-being model.

```{r ac wb model no ev}
tab_model(wb_ac_mods_no_ev$all_int, show.intercept = F, collapse.ci = F)
```


# Plot findings

## Fig 1. Change over time with individual pts and group trends

```{r fig 1}

# Recalculate models outside model function for easier plotting
bdi_plot_gc <- lmer(bdi_sz ~ year_cent5 + (1 + year_cent5 | ID), ylc, 
                    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 99999)))
wb_plot_gc <- lmer(wb_comp ~ year_cent5 + (1 + year_cent5 | ID), ylc, 
                   control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 99999)))

# Extract BDI fit line to superimpose on spaghetti plot
bdi_gc_plot_data <- Effect("year_cent5",
                           mod=bdi_plot_gc) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(fit = (((fit*0.264) + .508) ^2) - .01) # Backtransform and unstandardize BDI

# Extract WB fit line to superimpose on spaghetti plot
wb_gc_plot_data <- Effect("year_cent5",
                          mod=wb_plot_gc) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# BDI plot
dep_sp_tr <- ggplot(ylc, aes(x = year_cent5+5, y = bdi, color = ID, group = ID)) +
  geom_line(alpha = .3) +
  labs(title="A. Depression", 
       y = "BDI Mean", 
       x = "Year in Study") +
  theme_light() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1,3,5,7,9)) +
  theme(text=element_text(size=10), aspect.ratio=1.2, panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none") +
  geom_segment(x = 1, xend = 9, 
               y = bdi_gc_plot_data$fit[[1]], yend = bdi_gc_plot_data$fit[[5]], 
               linewidth=1.2, color = "black") 

# WB plot
wb_sp_tr <- ggplot(ylc, aes(x = year_cent5+5, y = wb_comp, color = ID, group = ID)) +
  geom_line(alpha = .3) +
  labs(title="B. Well-Being", 
       y = "Well-Being Composite", 
       x = "Year in Study") +
  theme_light() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1,3,5,7,9)) +
  theme(text=element_text(size=10), aspect.ratio=1.2, panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none") +
  geom_segment(x = 1, xend = 9, 
               y = wb_gc_plot_data$fit[[1]], yend = wb_gc_plot_data$fit[[5]], 
               linewidth=1.2, color = "black") 

# Display plots
grid.arrange(dep_sp_tr, wb_sp_tr, nrow = 1)
```

```{r fig 2}
f <- ggpredict(wb_com_mods$all_int, c("year_cent5", "com_val0_pmean[-0.31, 0.31]")) %>% 
  plot(alpha = 0.2, show_data = F, limits = c(-.40, .60)) + 
  scale_x_continuous(labels=function(x) x+5) +
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank()) +
  labs(title = "F. Well-Being",
       subtitle = "As a Function of \nCommunion Fulfillment",
       y = "Well-Being Composite",
       x = "Year",
       color = "Communion Fulfillment\n(Between-Person)") +
  theme_bw() + 
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1",
                      labels = c("-1 SD", "+1 SD"),
                      guide = guide_legend(reverse = T)) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())

grid.arrange(a,b,c,d,e,f, nrow = 3)
```
